0mwgscym7be5a47fd.name: Account takeover
0mwgscym7be5a47fd.summary: An attacker logs in as a real user, usually with stolen or guessed credentials.
signs: Logins from new countries or devices
Many failed attempts, then one success
Password or phone number changed right after login
steps: Lock the account and end all active sessions.
Reset the password and the recovery email and phone.
Review what the account did since the first odd login.
Reverse unauthorised actions and tell the account owner.
Turn on multi-factor sign-in for the account.

0mwgscym7d8eac7b7.name: Payment or transfer fraud
0mwgscym7d8eac7b7.summary: Money is moved out through transfers or payments the owner did not approve.
signs: Transfer volume far above normal
Large amounts split into smaller ones
Payee or bank details changed just before payment
steps: Hold or recall pending payments at once.
Ask the receiving bank to freeze the funds.
Confirm with the account owner by phone, not email.
Preserve logs and approval records for investigators.
Report to your bank, your regulator and the police where required.

0mwgscym71324de4b.name: Insider misuse
0mwgscym71324de4b.summary: A staff member or contractor uses their access for personal gain or to cause harm.
signs: Access to records outside their role
Activity at odd hours or during leave
Edits that skip the normal approval
steps: Quietly restrict the account’s access before any confrontation.
Preserve logs and copies of the affected records.
Involve HR and legal before speaking to the person.
Review what else the person could reach.
Close the control gap that allowed it.

0mwgscym7919d3436.name: Data theft
0mwgscym7919d3436.summary: Sensitive records are copied out of your systems.
signs: Bulk exports or downloads
Access to many unrelated records
Large uploads to personal storage or unknown addresses
steps: Cut off the account or connection doing the transfer.
Work out which records and which people are affected.
Preserve evidence and change any exposed credentials.
Notify your data protection regulator and affected people within the time your law requires.
Fix the access that made the copy possible.

0mwgscym799799891.name: Records tampering
0mwgscym799799891.summary: Balances, grades, invoices or logs are changed without proper approval.
signs: Edits with no matching approval
Changes to old, closed records
Gaps or deleted entries in audit logs
steps: Freeze the affected records.
Compare against a trusted backup and restore if needed.
Use the logs to find who changed what, and when.
Correct downstream reports and tell affected parties.
Require approval for edits to closed records.

0mwgscym7e5f90e78.name: Fake vendors or ghost workers
0mwgscym7e5f90e78.summary: Payments go to suppliers or employees who do not exist.
signs: Vendors added and paid within minutes
Different payees sharing a bank account or address
Staff on payroll with no attendance and no manager
steps: Pause payments to the suspect vendor or employee.
Verify they exist directly: ID check, site visit, call the supplier.
Trace who created and who approved the record.
Recover payments made and review similar records.
Separate duties so nobody can both create and approve a payee.

0mwgscym77e7d4bee.name: Phishing
0mwgscym77e7d4bee.summary: Staff are tricked into giving away passwords or approving fake requests.
signs: Staff report odd emails or links
Logins soon after a click
Emails asking to change bank details
steps: Find and remove the message from every inbox.
Reset passwords for anyone who clicked or replied.
Check those accounts for unusual activity.
Block the sender and the link addresses.
Warn staff using the real example.

0mwgscym790d0f481.name: Ransomware
0mwgscym790d0f481.summary: Malware locks your files and demands payment to unlock them.
signs: Files suddenly renamed or unreadable
Mass file changes in a short time
A ransom note on screens
steps: Disconnect affected machines from the network straight away.
Do not delete anything, and keep backups isolated.
Bring in your IT security team or a specialist.
Restore from clean backups.
Report the incident. Paying does not guarantee you get your files back.
